findings.text: The opening paragraph tells a newcomer what Athena is, who it is for and what problem it solves. The second paragraph explains why the page is a study of another project. A reader can answer "what is this and why does it matter" within the first screen.
findings.source: header, first lede: "Athena is an open-source system, written in Rust, that turns a short request into a change to a code repository."

findings.text: The title and heading are about firstmate, not Athena. A newcomer arriving at Athena's home URL may at first think they are on the wrong site or on a firstmate page, until they read the lede.
findings.source: <title> and h1: "Athena explains how firstmate handles work"

findings.text: The first section after the header is an error message. It sits exactly where a newcomer looks for proof that Athena works, and it undercuts the lede's promise of traceable models, cost and verdict.
findings.source: Check it on a real job: "The records of job 20261029-073603-7kqv could not be read here, so no models, verdict or costs are shown: no reading record for job 20261029-073603-7kqv."

findings.text: The next step is linked at the top, and the Next steps section gives concrete prerequisites, a clone command, `./setup.sh` and an example request. A newcomer knows what to do next.
findings.source: header: "Next step: install Athena or read firstmate itself" and Next steps: "athena ask \"add a changelog\""

findings.text: This link is aimed at the site owner, not a newcomer, and nothing explains it. It sits next to the newcomer's next-step link and may confuse a first-time reader.
findings.source: header: "Owner view: proposals waiting for your decision."

findings.text: The "Start here" section explains firstmate clearly. It defines its terms before using them and follows one piece of work from start to finish in plain steps.
findings.source: Start here: "Firstmate is a tool that keeps a backlog of programming tasks and hands each one to a separate AI coding tool, called a worker"

findings.text: Most of the page is a detailed state machine, plus 45 cited claims about firstmate's internals: exit codes, lock behaviour, pending-close replays. A newcomer judging Athena gets little from this depth. It works as evidence of thoroughness, not as an introduction.
findings.source: Transitions and Claims and sources sections (cards t1–t12, claims c1–c45)

findings.text: Several glossary entries say the source does not define the term. This is honest, but a newcomer is left with words they cannot fully understand.
findings.source: Glossary: "The firstmate source does not define a captain call." (also durable record, endpoint, heartbeat, wake)

findings.text: Several definitions appear twice, almost word for word, which makes an already long page longer for a first-time reader.
findings.source: Words used first / Glossary: duplicated entries for captain, yolo, in scope, green, red
